summary: The document is a non-functional placeholder containing seven highly ambiguous, subjective statements regarding a food delivery mobile app. It lacks all technical specifications, user roles, data models, security controls, and acceptance criteria, rendering it completely unusable for engineering or QA purposes.

risk_factors.title: Total Absence of Security Architecture
risk_factors.description: The document explicitly states 'No security requirements' and provides no guidance on authentication, authorization, data encryption, or API security for a system handling financial transactions and personal data.
risk_factors.mitigation: Implement a comprehensive security specification including OAuth2.0/OIDC for authentication, JWT for session management, TLS 1.3 for data in transit, AES-256 for data at rest, and OWASP Top 10 mitigation strategies for the mobile and backend layers.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Data Privacy and Compliance Framework
risk_factors.description: A food delivery app inherently collects PII (names, addresses, phone numbers) and PCI-DSS sensitive data (payment info). The document contains zero mention of GDPR, CCPA, or PCI-DSS compliance, creating immediate legal and financial liability.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define strict data retention policies, consent management workflows, and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements for the payment gateway integration. Specify data minimization principles and user rights for data deletion/export.

risk_factors.title: Unmeasurable Performance and SLA Requirements
risk_factors.description: Requirement #3 states 'Delivery should happen fast' and #2 states 'Food ordering must be easy'. These are subjective and untestable, leading to potential project failure due to lack of agreed-upon Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
risk_factors.mitigation: Define specific KPIs: e.g., 'API response time < 200ms for 95th percentile', 'Order confirmation within 5 seconds', 'Delivery ETA accuracy within +/- 10 minutes', and 'App crash rate < 0.1%'.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Payment Processing Logic
risk_factors.description: Requirement #4 'Customers can pay somehow' provides no detail on payment methods, currency support, refund logic, or third-party gateway integration, making it impossible to design the financial transaction flow.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify supported payment methods (Credit/Debit, Wallets, Cash on Delivery), integration with specific PSPs (e.g., Stripe, PayPal), idempotency keys for transaction safety, and detailed state machine for order payment status.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Replace with specific UX/UI guidelines, accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA), and performance benchmarks (e.g., 'App launch time < 2 seconds').
Define specific roles (Customer, Restaurant Admin, Delivery Driver, Super Admin) and map granular permissions for each, such as 'Restaurant Admin can update menu items and view daily sales reports'.
Specify notification channels (Push, SMS, Email), triggers (Order Placed, Driver Assigned, Out for Delivery, Delivered), and user preference settings for opt-in/opt-out.

Define the minimum viable reporting features for MVP (e.g., 'Daily sales summary for restaurant owners') and establish a data schema that supports future analytics, rather than deferring the data model design.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Without detailed functional requirements, developers cannot build the core features of ordering, tracking, or payment.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Detailed user stories for Customer, Restaurant, and Driver personas, including preconditions, postconditions, and edge cases (e.g., 'What happens if a restaurant rejects an order?').

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No definition of entities (User, Order, Item, Restaurant, Driver) or their relationships, leading to database design chaos.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram) defining tables, primary/foreign keys, data types, and constraints for all core entities.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No definition of how the mobile app, backend, and third-party services (maps, payments) will communicate.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: OpenAPI/Swagger specification for all REST/GraphQL endpoints, including request/response schemas, error codes, and rate limiting rules.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Lack of scalability, availability, and security standards will result in a fragile system that cannot handle real-world load.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specific metrics for concurrency (e.g., 'Support 10,000 concurrent users'), availability (e.g., '99.9% uptime'), and disaster recovery (RTO/RPO).

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The document explicitly states 'Not testable or measurable', making QA impossible.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Given/When/Then scenarios for each user story, unit test coverage targets, and integration test cases for critical paths (e.g., payment failure handling).

ai_recommendations: Reject this document immediately and initiate a formal requirements elicitation workshop with stakeholders to define specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) requirements.
Engage a Product Manager and Business Analyst to create a detailed Product Requirements Document (PRD) that includes user personas, user journeys, and a prioritized backlog (MoSCoW method).
Mandate the creation of a System Design Document (SDD) that covers architecture, data flow, security controls, and API contracts before any code is written.
